core_requests: P251 cond 1: adopt v3lum/modules/person_name/permute.py as v3lum/core/permute.py (shared offline helper for the e-mail pattern modules; modules may not add core files)

P251 cond 2: a read-only ctx view of the case (domains and observed e-mail addresses with their source module) so name_permutations can rank corporate formats from commit e-mails/public pages found by other modules (today: case seeds via options.seed_tlp, provenance path and org_profile only)

P251 cond 3/4: a 'generated' label on Pivot/Entity honoured by policy.decide (refuse breach, stealer, reputation and validation sinks for generated e-mails; username_check only after analyst selection) and a collapsible 'candidates (unverified guesses)' block in the renderers (WP14/WP20)

P121 cond 3: an in-memory core safe-archive member reader with caps (members, total inflated bytes, ratio, unsafe names) - v3lum.core.datasets.safe_extract only extracts to disk; x_archive_import uses stdlib zipfile in memory with the cond 3 caps meanwhile

P121 cond 2: a case-level evidence provenance record (e.g. `v3lum cases provenance <case> <file> --source --date --legal-basis`) readable through ctx; meanwhile the module requires an <archive>.provenance.json sidecar
P119 cond 1 / P333: add the X/Twitter status URL pattern to v3lum.core.patterns (detection/extraction label); x_twitter_public matches it itself (parse_status_url)

P120 cond 2: PROFILE_REQUIREMENTS binds *.wikipedia.org/*.wikimedia.org to 'V3LUM/{version} (+{contact}) python-requests' while P120 cond 2 writes 'V3LUM/<version> (<contact_email>)': architect decision to align them
username entities are lower-cased by the core normaliser; platform modules with case-sensitive names (MediaWiki) need the original case (e.g. an 'original' field)
notes: P119 is delivered as two modules in one file: x_twitter_public (status URLs via the published oEmbed interface) and x_twitter_recovery (username, run_on seeds, opt-in per run: selected with -M; usernames reach the unreviewed providers only on explicit selection with a purpose, POL-07). The syndication tweet-result adapter is not built and cdn.syndication.twimg.com is not registered (cond 2); twitter.com/x.com are not declared hosts (cond 3). Provider x_corp (new, hosts publish.twitter.com + publish.x.com, tier trusted, source oembed terms unknown); recovery uses the existing internet_archive.wayback_social source (terms unknown) and the shared P059 helpers of web_archives (parse_wayback_cdx, failure, CDX) plus the shared P314 decoder decode_platform_id (batch p2-G12-2, with a core-decoder fallback if that module is absent). oEmbed carries no numeric user id: only author handles become username pivots (cond 5 'user.id_str' needs the excluded syndication JSON). Wikimedia: provider wikimedia (new, meta/pt/en, trusted, open, P321 markers maxlag/ratelimited -> rate_limited and error objects -> error), contact UA from the core PROFILE_REQUIREMENTS template, contact_email empty or free-mail -> SKIPPED config before any request; IP lookups only for seeds and org_profile CIDRs; usernames keep counts/dates/case pages only. Wikimedia 200 fixtures are DOC-SHAPED (only a 429 is observable without the team contact UA): re-capture before default use (backlog). Acceptance route tests/fixtures/acceptance/ipv4/wikimedia.json uses the doc-shaped empty usercontribs answer. x_archive_import: offline, provenance sidecar <archive>.provenance.json required (SKIPPED config without it), in-memory stdlib zipfile reader with the cond 3 caps; username input is replaced by the provenance 'account_handle' comparison (single-entity runs). name_permutations: shared helper v3lum/modules/person_name/permute.py (core stand-in), cap 15 per kind (usernames, e-mails), maigret Permute strict adapted with MIT notice maigret_permutator. No LIGHT/ACTIVE variant is required by these final conditions. Registry contract test: the batch's five modules have no problems; failures seen in the full contract run belong to other batches in progress (disqus_profile, medium_feed, mojang_profile, pinterest_profile, snapchat_profile, stackexchange_user).
